# Section A
```{r}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/midwest_airbnb_extended.db")
listings     = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "listings") |> tibble::as_tibble()
availability = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "availability_monthly") |> tibble::as_tibble()
reviews      = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "reviews_monthly") |> tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

## Task 1
```{r}
host_counts = listings |>
  dplyr::count(host_id, name = "n_listings")

listings_hosts = listings |>
  dplyr::left_join(host_counts, by = "host_id")

# A1: how many hosts have 10+ listings (count HOSTS, not listing rows)
big_hosts = host_counts |> dplyr::filter(n_listings >= 10)
nrow(big_hosts)  # A1

# A2: percent of Chicago's listings held by those big hosts
listings_hosts |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Chicago") |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    pct_big_hosts = 100 * sum(n_listings >= 10) / dplyr::n()
  )  # A2

## Task 1 (all cities, for B2)
listings_hosts |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    pct_big_hosts = 100 * sum(n_listings >= 10) / dplyr::n()
  )

```

## Task 2
```{r}
family_listings = listings |>
  dplyr::filter(
    room_type == "Entire home/apt",
    accommodates >= 4,
    number_of_reviews >= 10,
    review_scores_rating >= 4.8
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(price_per_person = price / accommodates)

neighborhood_summary = family_listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, neighbourhood) |>   # check the exact column name in your data (neighbourhood vs neighborhood)
  dplyr::summarize(
    median_ppp = median(price_per_person, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(n >= 20)

neighborhood_summary |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Columbus") |>
  dplyr::arrange(median_ppp)  # A3 = top row's neighbourhood

```

## Task 3
```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, room_type) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    dplyr::across(
      c(price, reviews_per_month, estimated_revenue_l365d),
      ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
# A4 = the estimated_revenue_l365d value for Twin Cities + "Entire home/apt"
```


## Task 4
```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(estimated_revenue_l365d), .by_group = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    rank_in_city = dplyr::row_number(),
    cutoff = ceiling(0.10 * dplyr::n()),
    is_top10 = rank_in_city <= cutoff
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    pct_revenue_top10 = 100 * sum(estimated_revenue_l365d[is_top10], na.rm = TRUE) /
                         sum(estimated_revenue_l365d, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
# A5 = Columbus row
```


## Task 5
```{r}
oct_2026 = availability |> dplyr::filter(month == "2026-10")

entire_homes = listings |> dplyr::filter(room_type == "Entire home/apt")

oct_joined = entire_homes |>
  dplyr::inner_join(oct_2026, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(mostly_taken = nights_available < 0.5 * nights_in_month)

oct_joined |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    pct_mostly_taken = 100 * mean(mostly_taken, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(pct_mostly_taken)
# A6 = city in the top row; A7 = its pct_mostly_taken
```

## Task 6
```{r}
reviews_joined = reviews |>
  dplyr::inner_join(listings |> dplyr::select(id, city), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::filter(month >= "2025-07", month <= "2026-06")

monthly_totals = reviews_joined |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, month) |>
  dplyr::summarize(total_reviews = sum(reviews), .groups = "drop")

tc = monthly_totals |> dplyr::filter(city == "Twin Cities") |> dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(total_reviews))
tc  # A8 = top row's month
max(tc$total_reviews) / min(tc$total_reviews)  # A9

```


## Task 7
```{r}
superhost_summary = listings |>
  dplyr::filter(
    room_type == "Entire home/apt",
    host_is_superhost %in% c("t", "f")
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, host_is_superhost) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    median_price = median(price, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_rating = median(review_scores_rating, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
superhost_summary

```

## Task 8
```{r}
no_availability = listings |>
  dplyr::anti_join(availability, by = "id")

nrow(no_availability)  # A10
no_availability |> dplyr::count(city, sort = TRUE)  # tells you which city loses the most, for your README

```
